note: Set A is better because it contains significantly fewer incorrect claims. Both sets share specific misbinding errors (e.g., binding the refrigerator model to tag 'F1', assigning laminate dimensions to porcelain tile, and attributing tile colors to quartz), but Set B introduces numerous additional severe errors in the Finish Schedule, mixing attributes between Paint, Tile, and Glass items (e.g., assigning paint colors and finishes to tiles). While Set B extracts more correct equipment data, its high rate of hallucinated relationships makes it less reliable.
remarks: Both extractors struggle with the linearized text layer's lack of structural grouping, causing attribute bleeding between adjacent schedule items (e.g., Paint attributes binding to Tile entities). Set B's attempt at higher recall results in a disproportionately high false positive rate.
